rows.answer:
Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both, or with community service under Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (which replaced Section 500 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860). [1]

Related provisions:
- Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 covers defamation, printing or engraving defamatory matter, and the sale of printed or engraved substances containing defamatory matter, each punishable with simple imprisonment for a term extending to two years, or with fine, or with both [1].
- Section 222 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 covers prosecution for defamation upon a complaint made by some person aggrieved by the offence, or by the Public Prosecutor before a Court of Session in respect of public servants for conduct in the discharge of their public functions [5].
- Section 359 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (which replaced Section 320 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973) specifies that defamation under Section 356(2) may be compounded by the person defamed [2].

rows.question: When can a person accused of a non-bailable offence be released on bail?

rows.answer:
A person accused of a non-bailable offence may be released on bail when arrested or detained without a warrant by a police station officer in charge, or when they appear or are brought before a court other than the High Court or Court of Session, provided there are no reasonable grounds for believing they are guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, and they do not fall under prior conviction restrictions for certain major offences under Section 480 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (which replaced Section 437 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973) [1][3][8].

Conditions and time limits:
- The court may direct the release of a person accused of an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment, or with prior convictions, if that person is a child, a woman, sick, or infirm under Section 480 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 [1].
- The court may direct release for a person with prior convictions if satisfied it is just and proper for any other special reason under Section 480 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 [1].
